clue.text: Lumber a chap piled up in the Shard, for example

indicators.note: the two pieces are stacked one on the other in sequence, building the tower of the answer

parts.note: to lumber someone with a task is to land them with it
Mark is a typical man's name, so a chap

explanation.surface: Someone loads a man with timber stacked high in London's tallest skyscraper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shard is a skyscraper by London Bridge, the tallest building in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous building that stands out on the skyline is an example of a notable feature, a prominent sight.

clue.text: What astronauts have to make them use the stairs?

definitions.text: What astronauts have to make them use the stairs?

parts.words: What astronauts have to make them use the stairs?
parts.note: read as ..., with the elevator out of service, you would take the stairs

explanation.surface: A joke question about why spacemen climb stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The rocket's launch, read as a lift being switched off, explains the stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The moment a rocket leaves the ground is the launch every space crew experiences.

clue.text: It's no good engaging a hack

indicators.note: the N and G take the A between them

explanation.surface: A worthless journalist is being hired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' suggests a writer, but here it is an old horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a worn-out horse for riding, a poor old nag.

clue.text: Murderous graduate's hearing blown apart by police

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts graduate

indicators.note: the hearing word is split open with the police letters in it

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A graduate's court case is wrecked by detectives, in a deadly way.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing killing of one's mother is a specific kind of homicidal.

clue.text: Like an organ rebuilt near end of chapel

indicators.note: the word near is rebuilt with its letters in a new order
only the final letter of chapel is used

explanation.surface: A church instrument is restored close to the back of the chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: The organ is the kidney, not a church instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the kidneys, which are body organs.

clue.text: Setback here in Rome once in connection with award

parts.note: hic is the Latin word for here, spoken in ancient Rome
a cup is a trophy given as a prize

explanation.surface: A disappointment for someone in Rome long ago, concerning a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor hitch or interruption to progress is a small reverse, a temporary snag.

clue.text: Club represented by Falange extremists

parts.note: the outer letters of Falange are F and E, the chemical symbol for a metal that also names a golf club

explanation.surface: A political group is represented by hardliners of the Spanish fascist party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Falange was the Spanish fascist party; its extreme letters FE are the symbol of the metal named in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf club with a metal head is called by the metal's name.

clue.text: Supplied stew on credit? Only internally

indicators.note: the word for only goes inside the rearranged letters
to stew is to cook up, so the words are mixed into a new order

parts.note: but means only, as in but a moment

explanation.surface: A casserole provided on tick, but just its insides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' makes CONTRIED from ON CREDIT; 'internally' puts BUT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To have given money or help towards something is to have provided it.

clue.text: Contradictory statement a serviceman shortens in speech

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: the word is spoken rather than spelt, giving a same-sounding spelling

parts.note: to dock a tail is to shorten it

explanation.surface: A soldier talks in contradictions, cutting his words short.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-contradictory proposition that may yet be true is the classic logical puzzle.

clue.text: Gather in officers' place during island uprising

indicators.note: in a down entry the whole is written upwards, from the bottom
the mess sits within the island's letters

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile
the mess is where officers eat

explanation.surface: Troops muster in the officers' mess during a revolt on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns the whole combined string upwards, not just the island, which is fair in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To come together or bring together as a group is to convene.

clue.text: Maintain a stand, facing derision by ace in warplane

indicators.note: the ace and derision pieces sit inside the warplane word

parts.note: a fighter is a combat aircraft

indicators.note: derision comes by, that is next to and after, the ace piece

parts.note: an ace counts as one in cards
scorn is contempt, derision

explanation.surface: A fighter pilot keeps defending a position despite ridicule from his flying ace colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue hard for your own interests is to hold your position under pressure, the idiom from a boxer defending a ring corner.

clue.text: Sporting type's competition in ring

indicators.note: the competition word is placed inside the ring word

parts.note: the outer is the outermost ring of a target
the field is the set of competitors in an event

explanation.surface: An athlete enters a contest held in a boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielder stationed far out in cricket or baseball is a sportsperson, a player in a team game.

clue.text: Religious article placed before old soldier in pub

indicators.note: the article comes first in the down entry

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: the soldier goes inside the pub

parts.note: a local is your nearest pub
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A religious piece is put ahead of a veteran sitting in a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerning the study of God and doctrine relates to faith.

clue.text: One may secure an old railway poster

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former national railway
an ad is an advertisement, such as a poster

explanation.surface: Something could be used to fix a vintage railway advertisement to a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a description: one thing that may secure, i.e. fasten.
explanation.definitionFit: A brad is a small thin nail, which fastens or holds things in place.

clue.text: Remove subscriber's right? It's not intended

indicators.note: a letter is taken away from the subscriber word

parts.note: the undersigned is the person signing below, a subscriber

explanation.surface: A publisher cancels a member's entitlement, saying it was not deliberate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not planned or deliberate happened by accident.

clue.text: Maid regularly tucking into meat from the Low Countries

indicators.note: the regular letters are tucked inside the meat word

parts.note: flesh is the soft meat of an animal

indicators.note: every other letter of Maid is taken, starting from the first

explanation.surface: A servant is eating meat imported from the Netherlands or Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' suggests eating, but it signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Flemish describes Flanders, a region of Belgium, which lies in the Low Countries.

clue.text: Shelter in grass: concept welcomed at first

indicators.note: the concept and the first letter go inside the grass word

parts.note: hay is dried grass
an idea is a concept

indicators.note: only the opening letter of welcomed is used

explanation.surface: A refuge in the grass, an idea that was popular at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat or hiding place gives refuge.

clue.text: Overnight accommodation, neat like this?

parts.note: a B and B is bed and breakfast lodging
neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox

explanation.surface: A tidy guesthouse room is described as neat as can be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat as a bandbox' is a British idiom for very tidy; the clue asks for what something neat is like.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom neat as a bandbox makes the hatbox the standard of tidiness.

clue.text: Two ways to trap a web-footed bird

parts.note: a mall is a walkway or avenue
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Two routes are used to catch a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: The mallard is a common wild duck, a waterbird with webbed feet.

clue.text: Fusses over first of mites et al

indicators.note: only the initial letter of mites is taken

parts.note: et al is Latin for and others

explanation.surface: Someone frets about the leading insects and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To coddle and look after protectively, as a parent does.

clue.text: In the Spanish court providing cover for key journo

parts.note: el is the Spanish masculine definite article

indicators.note: the court piece stands in between the key and journo pieces, covering for a gap

parts.note: E is a musical key
an ed is an editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A Spanish court provides protection for an important journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the definition, as in voted in.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate who is voted in has been chosen at the ballot box.

clue.text: Material put on to protect English runner

indicators.note: the outer word surrounds and shields the inner pieces

parts.note: to don is to put on clothing
a ski runs over snow

explanation.surface: Fabric is worn to guard an English athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft leather or a fine woollen cloth made in imitation is a fabric.

clue.text: Remaining territory of some West Africans

definitions.meaning: the West African republic beside Ghana

explanation.surface: Land still held by certain people of West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means still left; as one it names a West African country.

clue.text: Jack a cheat? Nonsense

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, so jack gives tar
taken as written
to diddle is to swindle

explanation.surface: Is a sailor a swindler? Rubbish!
explanation.definitionFit: A taradiddle is a petty lie or pretentious nonsense, an old word for balderdash.

clue.text: In the morning one shot a friend in Uruguay

parts.note: am is ante meridiem, before noon
I is the Roman numeral one
a go is a try or shot

explanation.surface: Early one day someone shoots a companion in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish speakers, Uruguayans included, use this word for a pal.

clue.text: Paper briefly read in parliament

indicators.note: the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a daily is a newspaper published every day

explanation.surface: A newspaper is quickly read out in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the lower house of the Irish legislature, the Oireachtas.

clue.text: Former monk's chapter inserted oddly into gospel!

indicators.note: the chapter letter is inserted after the former piece within the monk's word

parts.note: ex means former
a lama is a Buddhist monk

indicators.note: the letters of into are arranged oddly

parts.note: Mark is one of the four gospels

clue.text: Member's verbal description of damage in Albert Square

explanation.walkthrough: Albert Square is the East London setting of the BBC soap EastEnders; a Cockney drops the H from harm.

clue.text: Thus a portraitist appears alone

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
Sir Peter Lely was a 17th-century portrait painter at the English court

explanation.surface: So a portrait painter turns up on his own.

clue.text: Forester's wife accepting chances half-heartedly

indicators.note: the wife word takes in the shortened chances

parts.note: a woman can mean a wife, as in his woman

indicators.note: one of the two central letters, the heart of the word, is lost

parts.note: odds are chances, probabilities

explanation.surface: A forestry worker's wife takes a gamble without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forester's' is the definition plus 's for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who works in or lives in a forest is a forest worker, a tree feller.
